stories.title: Nvidia reportedly halts AI server shipments to four Southeast Asian countries
stories.summary: Nvidia told manufacturing partners to stop shipping servers with its chips to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia, the Financial Times reported; Dell and Supermicro reportedly told buyers their orders can't ship.

stories.title: US chip curbs reportedly slow China's AI labs, with Moonshot's release gap set to double
stories.summary: Z.AI's next flagship model has fallen behind schedule and Moonshot AI expects the gap between its major releases could double from six months to a year or more, Reuters reported, citing sources, as US chip curbs and a distillation crackdown bite.

stories.title: Bank of Korea raises rates as the AI chip boom lifts growth
stories.summary: South Korea's central bank raised its benchmark rate by a quarter point to 3.25% amid higher-than-expected growth driven by the AI memory chip boom, and lifted its 2027 growth forecast to 4.1%.

stories.title: Denny's puts Jensen Huang's plaque back up after his return to Nvidia
stories.summary: After Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO, Denny's said it had restored the plaque honouring him that came down when he resigned, telling him 'your booth is waiting'.

stories.title: Musk pledges two SpaceX shares for every child in America
stories.summary: Elon Musk says every US child will get two SpaceX shares through Trump Accounts, one from SpaceX in December and one from him when his lockup ends in June 2027, a pledge worth about $18 billion at Wednesday's close.

predictions.note: A voluntary, single-company way to share AI-era gains: SpaceX and Musk put shares into every US child's Trump Account. Not yet an AI dividend policy.

stories.title: Dell's AI server backlog hits a record $132.3 billion
stories.summary: Dell's AI server revenue rose 291% from a year earlier to $22 billion in its third quarter to 30 October, and it ended the quarter with a record $132.3 billion AI backlog.

stories.title: FDA approves Neuralink's pivotal brain-implant trial for people with ALS
stories.summary: The FDA approved Neuralink's Link Pivotal Study, the first pivotal trial of an implantable brain-computer interface in the US, in people with severe paralysis from ALS; its earlier studies have over 30 implanted participants.

predictions.note: A regulator-approved pivotal trial moves implantable BCIs toward approved use, still far from high-bandwidth, two-way symbiosis.

stories.title: OpenAI says it has proved the speed limit for multiplying matrices
stories.summary: OpenAI posted a proof that the matrix multiplication exponent is 2.25, a limit on how efficient any algorithm for multiplying grids of numbers can be, New Scientist reported; no known algorithm reaches it yet.

stories.title: Hidden AI use hit at least 25 court cases in England and Wales this year
stories.summary: A Bureau of Investigative Journalism trawl shared with the Guardian found at least 25 cases in 2026 affected by undisclosed AI use, including AI-generated witness statements, fictitious case law and nonexistent statutes.

stories.title: Swiss officials say hackers used AI agents in five cyberattacks
stories.summary: Switzerland's cyber agency said five recent attacks on companies and critical-infrastructure operators used AI agents, and that in every case it knows of, the agents led to a successful compromise.

stories.title: Volvo trains Hexagon's AEON humanoid robots at its Ghent car plant
stories.summary: Volvo Cars is training Hexagon's wheeled AEON humanoids by imitation at its plant in Ghent, Belgium, ahead of a 2027 factory pilot, with real production use targeted from mid-2027.

predictions.note: One carmaker training humanoids ahead of a 2027 pilot: a step toward robots on live factory lines, not thousands at work yet.

stories.title: XPeng says its Iron humanoid will cost about as much as an electric car
stories.summary: XPeng's humanoid robots will cost roughly the same as an electric vehicle when they go on public sale in the second quarter of 2027, according to Bloomberg.

stories.title: ROBOTERA puts 45 humanoid robots to work at China Post's Hangzhou hub
stories.summary: ROBOTERA says 45 of its humanoid robots are deployed at China Post's Hangzhou Postal District Center, picking, reorienting and identifying parcels, after testing began in April.

predictions.note: Dozens of humanoids in live parcel operations at one postal hub: real work, but far short of thousands on factory lines.

stories.title: AGIBOT's X2 humanoid robots dance together as one team
stories.summary: AGIBOT showed multiple X2 humanoid robots dancing together, avoiding obstacles and changing formations, Interesting Engineering reported.

transcript.t: It's Friday, November 27, and this is the Singularity Daily.
Let's catch you up on the last 24 hours in superintelligence.
Who gets a seat at the table?
Nvidia has reportedly stopped shipping AI servers to four Southeast Asian countries.
Dell and Supermicro have reportedly told buyers their orders can't ship.
Washington wants top chips kept away from China, and Chinese labs are feeling it.
Z.ai's next big model is reportedly late.
Moonshot's gap between big releases could double, to a year.
In Korea, the AI memory chip boom has growth beating forecasts, so the central bank raised rates.
Oh, and Nvidia's boss is back, so Denny's put his plaque back up. His booth is waiting.
Now, the money.
Elon Musk says every child in America is getting two SpaceX shares.
One from SpaceX next month, one from Musk in June. That's about $18 billion.
Dell, meanwhile, has a record $132 billion of AI server orders still to fill.
Its AI server sales nearly quadrupled in a year, to $22 billion in one quarter.
Neuralink just got FDA approval for America's first pivotal trial of a brain implant, for people with ALS.
And OpenAI says it's proved the speed limit for multiplying grids of numbers, the math inside almost every computer.
The catch?
Hidden AI use has hit at least 25 court cases in England and Wales this year.
And Swiss officials say hackers used AI agents in five attacks.
So... is it so over?
We're so back!
Volvo's training humanoid robots at its plant in Ghent.
They learn the job by copying people.
They roll on wheels, carry parts, and could join real production from the middle of next year.
And XPeng says its humanoid will cost about the same as an electric car.
This Thanksgiving, don't just ask what the machines can do.
Ask who gets a seat at the table.
Zoom out, and the line only goes up.
Every day, the future shows up a little earlier.
All of that, in one day. And the days keep getting bigger.
You've been watching the Singularity Daily.
Go build something. See you tomorrow.
Want the whole month? Hear more tonight.
